groups.title: JavaScript Core Mechanics
groups.question: A teammate is confused that a Promise callback runs before a timer, and every click handler in a loop logs the same value. Explain how JavaScript runs async code and keeps variables.

followUps.Event Loop and Async Model: Why does a Promise callback run before a setTimeout of zero?
followUps.Closures and Scope Chain: Why might every handler created in a loop log the same value?

evidence.text: JavaScript runs one piece of code at a time on the call stack.
After the current code, all microtasks such as Promise callbacks run.
Only then does the next task, like a timer callback, run.

misconceptions.text: Says setTimeout with zero delay runs before any Promise callback.

evidence.text: A closure keeps access to the variables of the scope where it was created.
With var, every handler shares one variable, so they all see its final value.
let creates a new binding for each loop iteration, which fixes it.

groups.title: TypeScript Type System
groups.question: You are typing API data in a Nuxt app: an object from the server that must match an interface, and a helper that works with any entity that has an id. Explain the TypeScript behind this.

followUps.Structural Typing vs Nominal Typing: Why does an object satisfy an interface it was never declared with?
followUps.Generic Constraints and Inference: How do generic constraints keep a helper flexible but safe?

evidence.text: TypeScript checks the shape of a value, not its declared name.
Any object with the required properties is accepted.
Nominal typing, used in some languages, would require an explicit declaration.
A generic lets a function work with many types while keeping them linked.
extends restricts the type, for example to types with an id.
TypeScript usually infers the type from the arguments, so callers rarely write it.

groups.title: Node.js Runtime Essentials
groups.question: A Nuxt server route reads a large file into memory and crashes, and an old package fails to import. Explain Node's module systems and streams.

followUps.Module System: ESM vs CommonJS: How do ES modules and CommonJS differ, and why does mixing them cause errors?
followUps.Streams and Buffer Handling: Why use streams for large files?

evidence.text: CommonJS uses require and module.exports; ES modules use import and export.
ES modules are analysed before running, while require runs at runtime.
They are not fully interchangeable, so mixing them needs care.
Streams process data piece by piece.
They avoid loading the whole file into memory.
They suit uploads, downloads and large data processing.

groups.title: Async Patterns in Practice
groups.question: Your Nuxt server code sometimes fails silently and some errors never reach your logs. Explain how errors flow through async code.

followUps.Promise Chaining vs async/await: What goes wrong when you forget to await a Promise?
followUps.Error Propagation in Async Code: Why do unawaited Promises hide errors, and how does Promise.all behave on failure?

evidence.text: async/await is a cleaner way to work with Promises.
Without await, the code continues before the work finishes.
Errors from awaited calls are caught with try and catch.
Errors only reach your try and catch when the Promise is awaited.
Unawaited Promises can fail without anyone noticing.
Promise.all rejects as soon as one fails, while allSettled waits for all and reports each result.
